Can Judgment Be Good News?

What comes to mind when you hear the word “judgment”?

You may imagine a courtroom, punishment, public shame, or someone searching for a reason to reject you.

Human courts can make mistakes. Evidence can be hidden. Powerful people may receive special treatment. A person’s story may be ignored because of race, money, family name, or social position.

The Creator’s judgment is different.

He cannot be bribed, deceived, pressured, or influenced by prejudice. He knows every action, motive, opportunity, wound, and hidden truth.

His judgment exposes evil, defends those who have been wronged, and shows that His decisions are completely fair.

For those who trust Jesus, judgment is not a reason to live in terror. Jesus is both Judge and Advocate. The One examining your life is the same One who gave His life to save you.

Why Is a Judgment Necessary?

The conflict between good and evil began with accusations against the Creator.

Satan claimed that God was unfair, controlling, and unworthy of trust. The history of our world has allowed everyone to see the results of Satan’s way and God’s way.

Before evil ends, the Creator opens the record.

Read Daniel 7:9–10 ↗.

Daniel saw a heavenly courtroom. The court was seated, and books were opened.

The judgment shows:

  • That the Creator has told the truth
  • That His law is fair
  • That Jesus has provided complete salvation
  • That each person received freedom to choose
  • That God has forgiven everyone who sincerely came to Him
  • That those who remain lost continually rejected His grace
  • That every final decision is just

The judgment is not held because God needs help remembering what happened. He already knows everything.

The records are opened so that the beings watching the conflict can understand His decisions.

The Creator Sees What Human Systems Miss

Read Ecclesiastes 12:13–14 ↗.

God will bring every work into judgment, including hidden things.

This includes secret acts of kindness that no one noticed. It also includes hidden cruelty that no one held accountable.

No victim is forgotten.

No lie can remain hidden forever.

No powerful person can destroy the evidence.

No one can silence the Creator’s testimony.

Read Psalm 9:7–10 ↗.

God judges the world with righteousness. He becomes a refuge for people who have been oppressed.

The Creator’s judgment means that injustice does not receive the final word.

What Are the Books of Judgment?

The Bible describes heavenly records using the picture of books.

The Book of Life

Read Philippians 4:3 ↗ and Revelation 3:5 ↗.

The Book of Life contains the names of people who have entered a relationship with the Creator.

Having a name recorded there is not based on race, family background, social position, or membership in a human institution.

It is based on receiving the life Jesus offers.

The record of our lives

Read Revelation 20:12 ↗.

The Bible says people are judged according to what is written in the books.

The Creator has a complete record of human life. He sees actions that were public and choices that were private.

Read Matthew 12:36–37 ↗ and 1 Corinthians 4:5 ↗.

He also understands words, motives, and the hidden purposes of the heart.

These records are always accurate. The Creator never misunderstands what happened.

Are We Saved by Our Actions?

Read Ephesians 2:8–10 ↗.

We are saved by grace through faith, not by earning enough good marks in the record.

Why, then, does the judgment examine our actions?

Actions reveal whether faith is alive.

An apple tree does not become an apple tree by producing apples. It produces apples because it is an apple tree.

In the same way, loving and obedient actions do not purchase salvation. They show the results of a real relationship with Jesus.

Read James 2:17–18 ↗ and Matthew 7:16–20 ↗.

A person may claim to follow God while continually choosing dishonesty, cruelty, or rebellion. The judgment reveals whether that claim was real.

The Creator does not look for a flawless human record. He looks for evidence that we have trusted Jesus, responded to the Holy Spirit, and allowed grace to work in our lives.

What Standard Does the Creator Use?

Read James 2:10–12 ↗.

James calls God’s law the law of liberty and says we will be judged by it.

The Ten Commandments reveal the Creator’s standard of love. They show how love behaves toward God and toward people.

Read Ecclesiastes 12:13–14 ↗.

The same standard applies to everyone.

No culture, government, church, leader, family, or individual has permission to rewrite the Creator’s moral law.

The law reveals sin. Jesus provides forgiveness. The Holy Spirit gives us power to live differently.

Does the Creator Consider Each Person’s Circumstances?

The Creator judges everyone by the same truth, but He also understands every person completely.

Read Luke 12:47–48 ↗.

Jesus taught that responsibility is connected to the knowledge and opportunities a person received.

God knows:

  • What truth you were taught
  • What truth was kept from you
  • Whether someone misrepresented Him
  • What choices were available to you
  • What pressure you experienced
  • What pain affected your decisions
  • What you understood at the time
  • How you responded when more truth became clear

This does not make harmful choices harmless. It means the Creator understands every case more fully than any human judge could.

Read Genesis 18:25 ↗.

The Judge of all the earth will do what is right.

When Does the Judgment Take Place?

Many people assume that every part of the judgment happens after Jesus returns.

The Bible shows that one phase begins before His return.

Read Daniel 7:9–14 ↗.

Daniel saw the heavenly court sit in judgment. After the judgment began, Jesus received His kingdom.

Read Daniel 7:21–22 ↗.

The judgment resulted in a decision in favor of God’s faithful people. Then the time came for them to receive the kingdom.

The order is important:

  1. The heavenly court sits.
  2. The books are opened.
  3. Lives are examined.
  4. Jesus receives the kingdom.
  5. God’s people inherit the kingdom.

Read Revelation 22:12 ↗.

When Jesus returns, He brings His reward with Him. A decision must already have been reached before the reward can be given.

This first phase is often called the pre-advent judgment because it takes place before the Second Coming.

What Is the Heavenly Sanctuary?

To understand the timing of the judgment, we need to understand the sanctuary.

Read Exodus 25:8–9 ↗.

God instructed Israel to build a sanctuary so He could live among them. Its services taught people about sin, forgiveness, Jesus’ sacrifice, and the removal of sin.

The earthly sanctuary had two main rooms:

  • The Holy Place
  • The Most Holy Place

Priests served daily in the first part. Once each year, on the Day of Atonement, the high priest entered the Most Holy Place for a special work of cleansing and judgment.

Read Leviticus 16:29–34 ↗.

The earthly sanctuary was a teaching model of a greater sanctuary in heaven.

Read Hebrews 8:1–2 ↗ and Hebrews 9:23–24 ↗.

Jesus is our High Priest in the true heavenly sanctuary. After His resurrection and return to heaven, He began serving on humanity’s behalf.

The sacrifice was completed at the cross. His heavenly ministry applies the benefits of that sacrifice to everyone who comes to Him.

What Does It Mean to Cleanse the Sanctuary?

During the earthly sanctuary service, confessed sins were symbolically transferred to the sanctuary through the blood of sacrifices.

Once each year, the sanctuary was cleansed.

Read Leviticus 16:15–22 ↗.

This yearly Day of Atonement represented the Creator’s final work of judgment and removal of sin.

The animal sacrifices could never save anyone. They pointed forward to Jesus.

Read Hebrews 10:1–14 ↗.

Jesus offered one complete sacrifice for sin. The cleansing of the heavenly sanctuary does not mean that heaven became morally dirty. It refers to the final review and removal of the record of confessed sin.

The Creator does not plan to keep the record of forgiven sin forever.

Read Acts 3:19 ↗.

God promises that sins can be blotted out.

What Is the 2,300-Day Prophecy?

Read Daniel 8:13–14 ↗.

Daniel was told that the sanctuary would be cleansed after 2,300 prophetic days.

This vision included symbolic animals representing kingdoms and events extending far beyond Daniel’s lifetime. The time period must therefore represent more than 2,300 ordinary days.

The Bible sometimes uses one prophetic day to represent one literal year.

Read Numbers 14:34 ↗ and Ezekiel 4:6 ↗.

Using this day-for-a-year principle, the 2,300 days represent 2,300 years.

Daniel did not understand this part of the vision.

Read Daniel 8:26–27 ↗.

The angel had explained the symbols, but the time period remained unresolved. Daniel became ill and said he was astonished by the vision.

When Did the 2,300 Years Begin?

Read Daniel 9:20–25 ↗.

Gabriel returned and helped Daniel understand the earlier vision.

He said that 70 prophetic weeks were determined for Daniel’s people and that the period would begin with a command to restore and rebuild Jerusalem.

Seventy prophetic weeks contain 490 days. Using the prophetic day-for-a-year principle, they represent 490 years.

The decree that fully restored Jerusalem’s civil and religious government was issued by the Persian king Artaxerxes in 457 B.C.

Read Ezra 7:11–26 ↗.

This date becomes the starting point for both the 490-year period and the larger 2,300-year prophecy.

How Did the Prophecy Point to Jesus?

Daniel 9 ↗ said that 69 prophetic weeks would reach from the decree to the appearance of the Messiah.

Sixty-nine weeks contain 483 prophetic days, representing 483 years.

Beginning in 457 B.C., the 483 years reach to A.D. 27 because there is no year zero between 1 B.C. and A.D. 1.

In A.D. 27, Jesus was baptized and publicly began His work.

Read Luke 3:1–3 ↗, Luke 3:21–22 ↗, and Acts 10:37–38 ↗.

Daniel also said that the Messiah would bring sacrifice and offering to an end in the middle of the final prophetic week.

Read Daniel 9:26–27 ↗.

Three and a half years after His baptism, Jesus died in the spring of A.D. 31. His death completed what the animal sacrifices had represented.

Read Matthew 27:50–51 ↗.

When Jesus died, the curtain in the temple was torn from top to bottom. The earthly sacrificial system had reached its fulfillment.

The final three and a half years extended to A.D. 34, completing the 490 years given especially to Daniel’s people. The message then moved outward with new force to other nations.

Why Is 1844 Important?

The first 490 years were part of the longer 2,300-year period.

After subtracting 490 years from 2,300 years, 1,810 years remain.

The 490 years ended in A.D. 34. Adding the remaining 1,810 years brings us to 1844.

The prophecy can be summarized this way:

  • 457 B.C.: The decree to restore Jerusalem
  • A.D. 27: Jesus is baptized and begins His public work
  • A.D. 31: Jesus dies in the middle of the final prophetic week
  • A.D. 34: The 490-year period ends
  • 1844: The full 2,300-year period ends

Daniel 8:14 ↗ says that at the end of this period, the sanctuary would be cleansed.

The heavenly phase of judgment therefore began in 1844.

Did Jesus Return in 1844?

Some sincere Bible students expected Jesus to return in 1844.

They correctly calculated the ending date of the prophecy, but they misunderstood the event.

They assumed the sanctuary was Earth and that its cleansing meant the world would be cleansed by fire when Jesus returned.

The Bible identifies the sanctuary involved in this final work as the sanctuary in heaven.

Read Hebrews 8:1–2 ↗ and Hebrews 9:24 ↗.

Jesus did not return to Earth in 1844. He entered the final phase of His ministry as our High Priest in the heavenly sanctuary.

This is the work represented by the Day of Atonement: judgment, cleansing, and the final removal of sin.

A correct date does not make every interpretation of the event correct. Scripture must explain both the time and what happens when that time ends.

Whose Lives Are Examined?

Read 1 Peter 4:17 ↗.

The judgment begins with those who have claimed to belong to God.

It does not examine people so God can discover information He did not know. It reveals who truly chose a saving relationship with Jesus.

A name may appear on a membership list while the heart remains far from God. Another person may have little public recognition while living with sincere faith.

The Creator sees the difference.

Read 2 Timothy 2:19 ↗.

He knows those who are His.

The Bible does not tell us when any particular person’s case is examined. It calls every generation to live in a ready relationship with Jesus.

Is Jesus Your Judge or Your Advocate?

He is both.

Read John 5:22 ↗ and Acts 17:31 ↗.

The Father has committed judgment to Jesus.

Read 1 John 2:1–2 ↗.

Jesus is also our Advocate. An advocate stands beside someone and speaks on that person’s behalf.

The Judge is the One who died for you.

The Advocate is the One who knows every charge.

The evidence of His sacrifice is complete.

Read Hebrews 7:24–25 ↗.

Jesus lives to intercede for those who come to God through Him.

If you have confessed your sins and placed your life in His hands, you do not stand in the judgment alone.

What Does Jesus Present for You?

Your record cannot save you. Even your best actions cannot erase one sin.

Jesus presents His own perfect life and sacrifice for everyone who truly belongs to Him.

Read Zechariah 3:1–5 ↗.

The prophet saw Joshua the high priest standing in dirty clothing while Satan accused him.

The Creator ordered the dirty clothing removed and gave Joshua clean clothing.

The dirty clothing represented sin. The clean clothing represented the righteousness the Creator provides.

Satan points to your worst choices and says you should be rejected.

Jesus does not pretend that the choices were acceptable. He points to His sacrifice, removes the guilt of confessed sin, and covers you with His righteousness.

Your hope in the judgment is Jesus.

What Happens to Confessed Sin?

Read 1 John 1:9 ↗.

When you confess your sin, the Creator forgives and cleanses you.

Read Psalm 32:1–5 ↗.

David described the relief that came when he stopped hiding and confessed.

During the judgment, the record shows that the sin was covered by the sacrifice of Jesus.

At the conclusion of the judgment, confessed and forsaken sins are blotted from the record.

The Creator does not expose forgiven sin to humiliate you. His plan is to remove it forever.

What About Sin We Refuse to Surrender?

Grace does not force anyone to remain with the Creator.

A person may claim to follow Jesus while continually protecting sin and refusing the Holy Spirit’s call to repent.

Read Hebrews 10:26–29 ↗.

This passage is not describing someone who struggles, falls, confesses, and returns to Jesus. It describes a deliberate decision to reject the only sacrifice that can save.

Read Revelation 3:5 ↗.

Jesus promises not to blot the names of those who overcome from the Book of Life.

The promise also shows that names can be removed when people finally reject their relationship with Him.

The Creator respects human freedom. He will not record someone as His faithful child while that person has chosen to leave Him permanently.

Can You Have Assurance During the Judgment?

Yes.

Read Romans 8:1 ↗.

There is no condemnation for those who remain in Jesus.

Read John 6:37 ↗.

Jesus will not turn away anyone who comes to Him.

Read 1 John 5:11–13 ↗.

You can know that you have eternal life through Jesus.

Assurance does not come from pretending you never sin. It comes from staying honest with the Creator, trusting Jesus, confessing when you fall, and continuing to follow Him.

You do not need to spend every day wondering whether God is searching for a reason to reject you.

Jesus is working to save everyone who allows Him.

Why Do Our Choices Still Matter?

Read 2 Corinthians 5:10 ↗.

The judgment examines how each person lived.

Our choices show what we truly value.

A single failure does not define an entire life. A hidden act of kindness does not purchase salvation. The complete record reveals the direction of the heart.

The Creator sees:

  • Whether we accepted correction
  • Whether we confessed when we were wrong
  • Whether we practiced mercy
  • Whether our faith produced action
  • Whether we used power to serve or control
  • Whether we treated people with dignity
  • Whether we followed the truth we understood
  • Whether we continued choosing Jesus

Works are the evidence. Grace is the basis of salvation.

What Are the Three Phases of Judgment?

The Bible presents three phases.

Before the Second Coming: review

The heavenly court examines the lives of those who have claimed a relationship with God.

Read Daniel 7:9–10 ↗ and Revelation 14:6–7 ↗.

This phase began in 1844 and takes place before Jesus returns.

During the thousand years: understanding

After Jesus returns, His saved people participate in reviewing the judgment of the lost and the fallen angels.

Read Revelation 20:4–6 ↗ and 1 Corinthians 6:2–3 ↗.

This review answers questions. The saved will understand why certain people are absent and why every decision was fair.

After the thousand years: final judgment

At the end, every lost person will see the complete truth.

Read Revelation 20:11–15 ↗.

The final sentence will be carried out, and sin will be removed from the universe.

The next guide will examine what happens to the wicked and why the Creator does not keep people suffering forever.

When Will the Judgment End?

The Bible does not give us a date.

There will come a point when every decision is final and Jesus completes His work in the heavenly sanctuary.

Read Revelation 22:11–12 ↗.

After that point, Jesus returns with His reward.

No visible announcement tells the world that an individual case is being considered. That is why Scripture says today is the time to respond.

Read Hebrews 3:7–8 ↗.

Do not harden your heart when the Holy Spirit speaks.

The Creator is not trying to frighten you into a rushed emotional choice. He is inviting you to stop delaying a relationship you know you need.

How Should the Judgment Change the Way You Live?

Live honestly

You do not need to maintain a spiritual appearance. Bring your real life to the Creator.

Confess quickly

When the Holy Spirit reveals sin, do not hide or defend it. Confess and receive forgiveness.

Make wrongs right

When possible, apologize, return what was taken, repair harm, and change your behavior.

Treat people with dignity

The Creator sees how we treat people with less power, influence, or social protection.

Use your time with purpose

Your life matters. Your choices are becoming part of your permanent story.

Trust Jesus

The purpose of judgment is not to make you your own savior. Your only safe place is in Jesus.

What If Religious Judgment Has Hurt You?

People may have judged your appearance, family, culture, questions, or past while knowing very little about your life.

They may have confused their preferences with the Creator’s commands.

Human condemnation is not the same as God’s judgment.

Read 1 Samuel 16:7 ↗.

People look at outward appearances. The Creator sees the heart.

God will not judge you by stereotypes, rumors, or another person’s prejudice. He knows your true story.

He will also judge those who used His name to shame, exploit, or abuse others.

You can place both your life and the wrongs committed against you in the hands of a completely fair Judge.
